work.subtitle: 合成入口事件分析报告
work.framework: report: Source and interpretation / distinct native A4 document layout
work.scope: Entirely synthetic teaching report: 240 entry events, not unique people, occupancy, actual observations, weather or causal evidence.

pages.title: Report the model, not a real place.
pages.lead: PUBLIC THREAD describes a deterministic teaching model with 240 invented entry-event records. The coastal scenes are visual context, not a collection site.
pages.body: Daily model totals are 42, 50, 46, 58 and 44. Segment totals are 70, 80 and 90. Both margins describe the same records and reconcile to 240.

pages.title: Follow the report structure.
pages.lead: Read source definition before summary, variation and interpretation. Keep the unit attached to every number even when a chart or table is shared separately.
pages.body: Pages 3–4 define records and margins; pages 5–7 compare totals and summaries; pages 8–9 describe limitations and handoff; page 10 supplies the source note.

pages.title: An event is not a person.
pages.lead: One row represents one invented entry event. A unique record ID identifies the row, not a distinct visitor. No identity, exit or duration field exists.
pages.body: Repeated entries by a real person could produce multiple events in an actual study. This source cannot calculate unique visitors, dwell time or live occupancy.

pages.title: Reconcile the two margins.
pages.lead: The day totals sum to 42 + 50 + 46 + 58 + 44 = 240. The three segment totals sum to 70 + 80 + 90 = 240.
pages.body: Adding the two grand totals would double-count the same source model. The deterministic joint allocation illustrates bookkeeping, not an empirical relationship between day and place.

pages.title: Describe a difference without a cause.
pages.lead: Tuesday has 50 model events and Monday has 42, a difference of eight. The source supplies no programme, weather or intervention variable.
pages.body: The difference is a bounded description of invented values. It cannot explain an effect of weather, a design change, an event or a real operational decision.

pages.title: State the mean with its scope.
pages.lead: The five daily totals sum to 240, giving a mean of 48 events per model day label. The model has no real observation dates or hours.
pages.body: The arithmetic is correct for this source, but 48 is not a forecast or capacity target. Equal observation coverage and an events-per-hour denominator cannot be verified.

pages.title: Keep variation visible.
pages.lead: Sorting the five day totals gives 42, 44, 46, 50 and 58. The median is 46 and the range is 58 minus 42, or 16.
pages.body: These summaries lose information about labels and order. The range is not a confidence interval or a guaranteed bound for a future real observation.

pages.title: Missing is not an observed zero.
pages.lead: No weekend, duration, person identity or contextual variable is supplied. An absent period or field is unknown, not a measured zero.
pages.body: Do not fill a table with guessed values to make it appear complete. State the boundary beside the result rather than relying on an appendix that may be separated from it.

pages.title: Hand over a bounded finding.
pages.lead: A responsible summary states source, unit, scope and limitation before suggesting a next question. It does not turn an attractive harbor image into evidence.
pages.body: Suggested sentence: In this synthetic model, Thursday has 58 of 240 entry events; the source does not explain why. That statement describes the set without predicting demand.

pages.title: Retain the complete source note.
pages.lead: All rows are deterministically constructed teaching records. No observer visited the fictional location and no count was inferred from a drawn person.
pages.body: The source CSV/JSON included with this case preserve all 240 records. IDs distinguish events only. A real investigation would require a separate method and responsible review.
